Services
Shinkansen (JR East)
Officially an intermediate station on the Tōhoku Shinkansen, the following also operate:
Hokkaidō Shinkansen: through services from Shin-Aomori to Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto.
Akita Shinkansen: a mini-Shinkansen using the narrow-gauge Tazawako Line and Ōu Main Line between this station and Akita. E5 "Hayabusa" and E6 "Komachi" sets couple and uncouple here.

Conventional lines
Officially the following four conventional lines:
Tōhoku Main Line (JR East) — the station to which JR East assigns this station; it is the terminus.
Tazawako Line (JR East) — nominally the terminus, with the 0 km post in the station; operationally trains from here are down services. It was regauged to standard gauge for the Akita Shinkansen through services.
Yamada Line (JR East) — this station is the origin. Until the March 2018 revision, trains from here used even numbers even though they were down services; after the March 23, 2019 transfer of the Miyako–Kamaishi section to Sanriku, from the March 2018 revision Morioka-origin down services officially use odd numbers.
Iwate Galaxy Railway Line (IGR Iwate Galaxy Railway) — this station is the origin.

Operationally the following also run:
Hanawa Line (JR East) — officially originating at Kōma, but all trains run through the Iwate Galaxy Railway Line to this station.
Kamaishi Line (JR East) — officially originating at Hanamaki, but all Rapid Hamayuri and some local trains run through the Tōhoku Main Line to this station.

Station layout
The station has five conventional-line platforms serving ten tracks (Platforms 0–9) and two Shinkansen island platforms serving four tracks (Platforms 11–14), totaling seven platforms and fourteen tracks. The conventional platforms reflect the days when many named trains called; the number of at-grade platforms is the largest in the Tōhoku region and each platform is long. With the transfer of the Morioka – Hachinohe Tōhoku Main Line to IGR during Shinkansen extension to Hachinohe, Platforms 0/1 became dedicated to IGR and JR Hanawa Line services. Except for Tazawako Line platforms 8/9, all yard movements and Morioka Rolling Stock Center entry/exit are managed by JR Morioka Transportation Headquarters (Platforms 8/9 come under the Akita transport control).

The station (including free passages) is fully closed between 0:00 and 4:45.

On the 2nd floor are the souvenir shop "Daichikan" and the "Iwate antenna shop".

JR East
The 2nd floor is the concourse, connected to the west exit by the east-west free passage "Sansa Komichi" (former Tazawako Line substitute-bus footbridge). On the concourse are the south gate, north gate, and two Midori no Madoguchi (one north, one south). Reserved-seat ticket machines are at each. JR automatic ticket machines can sell single tickets to Iwate-Numakunai on the Iwate Galaxy Railway Line, but not to Hanawa Line stations via that line (except Kōma). The gates use Suica-compatible automatic readers, and the Shinkansen gate supports Shinkansen e-ticket. Plasma displays at the gates show real-time train information.

On the south side are a combined waiting lounge, a North-Tōhoku tourist plaza and an information center (Lex Go service / train delivery service), the latter outsourced to JR East Tōhoku General Service.

It is a directly managed and management station, supervising Hizume – Senboku on the Tōhoku Main Line, Maegata – Akabuchi on the Tazawako Line, Kami-Morioka – Sentoku on the Yamada Line, and Higashi-Ōgae – Anikubo on the Hanawa Line. It previously also supervised Ōjita and Asashi, but both closed on March 25, 2016.

Average daily passengers in fiscal 2022: 14,610 (including IGR interchanges), the highest of any station in Iwate. Shinkansen average daily passengers: 5,923.

In JR East station passenger rankings it does not reach the top 100 because commuter volumes are smaller than in metropolitan areas, but in operating revenue rankings, long-distance Shinkansen traffic places it near the top outside the Kantō region, after Sendai and Niigata (18th in fiscal 2018).

Conventional line platforms
At-grade (bridge) station with four island platforms serving eight tracks.

Platforms

Hanawa Line trains (except some) use Iwate Galaxy Railway platforms (0/1) (see below).

Platform 3 is the up main and Platform 4 the down main, so both are mainly used by freight trains passing or stopping.

From Platforms 0–7, crossovers allow entry to and exit from Morioka Rolling Stock Center; the section to the center is triple-track (IGR up/down mains and depot track). The depot track was formerly double but was singled during Akita Shinkansen construction to provide right-of-way for the divergence viaduct; it becomes double again inside the depot.

Platforms 8/9 are standard gauge for the Tazawako Line. Normally used only by Tazawako Line local trains, on days of the National Fireworks Competition (Daisen City), temporary Komachi services starting/terminating here (not through to the Shinkansen) also use them. On the north side of the yard are storage tracks for standard-gauge trains, and on the west side a track with overhead gantries for inspection.

Next to Platform 9 is a narrow-gauge track without a platform (down Platform 6), used by down freight trains waiting; it crosses the standard-gauge tracks at grade on the north side.

From February to March 2014, gypsum suspended ceilings on the conventional-line central footbridge were removed due to seismic concerns, completed by mid-March. At the same time, departure signs at the conventional south gate were replaced with the same new LED type as the north gate, and all platform departure signs were updated to LED.

Shinkansen platforms
Elevated (3rd floor above ground) station with two island platforms serving four tracks.

In the current timetable all trains stop, but the up/down main platforms 12/13 are built to profile for passing, with the gap from track center to platform edge 3 cm wider than on sidings 11/14.

All scheduled Komachi services couple/uncouple with Hayabusa here.

The divergence between the Akita and Tōhoku Shinkansen lies about 500 m north of Morioka. A switch is provided only on the down main, so up Komachi trains first enter the down main and then cross to the up main via a connecting track before entering Morioka. Unlike Fukushima, where coupling/uncoupling takes place on the same platform, down uncoupling takes place on Platform 14 and up coupling on Platform 11 (both outer platforms).

From November to early December 2012, Shinkansen concourse departure signs were replaced with full-color LED type, and gate departure signs were replaced with LCD displays on December 11–12. LED position markers were installed on all platforms 11–14 (Platforms 12/13 in the 2008 revision, Platforms 13/14 for the 2016 Hokkaido Shinkansen opening). Simplified markers were once on Platforms 11/14.

Morioka is the northernmost station on the Tōhoku Shinkansen capable of handling 17-car trains.

Since November 1, 2019, the departure melody has been Masataka Azuma's "Daijōbu", theme song of the TV drama "Dondon Haré" set in Morioka. Originally scheduled until October 31, 2021, it was continued due to popularity.

Platforms

On the Shinkansen platforms are the "NewDays KIOSK Morioka Shinkansen Platform" shop, JR East Tōhoku General Service shops and several ekiben vendors. NewDays KIOSK uses former closed shops on platforms 11/12; after a trial from November 28 to December 10, 2019, it opened full-time on December 11.

IGR Iwate Galaxy Railway
At-grade station with one bay platform serving two tracks, on the north side of the 1st floor of the station building. JR Hanawa Line trains via the Iwate Galaxy Line to Kōma also mainly use this platform. It is not possible to transfer within the paid area to other lines; the IGR gate is about 200 m (about 8 minutes walk) from the JR north gate. This platform was rebuilt and renamed from the former JR Platform 1 and the up freight track (no platform number).

It is a directly managed station with a general stationmaster and assistant. There are waiting rooms inside and outside the gate, a ticket gate, ticket windows and automatic ticket machines. The ticket machines can sell through tickets as far as Hachinohe on the Aoimori Railway, Same on the Hachinohe Line, and Ōdate on the Hanawa Line. Outside the gate are NewDays and station-building shops. It supervises Aoyama – Mido stations.

Hanawa Line trains are worked through between this station and Ōdate by JR East Morioka Transport Room drivers and conductors; no crew change is made at the company boundary Kōma. Through Aoimori Railway drivers are worked through between this station and Hachinohe by IGR or Aoimori drivers; no crew change is made at the company boundary Metoki.

Some trains use JR platforms, in which case the JR gate must be used.

Platforms

Renovation work
The basement and 1st floor dated from the late-1950s first Tōhoku minshū eki, and the 2nd floor from the 1982 Tōhoku Shinkansen opening. Under the JR East Station Renaissance project, Morioka City barrier-free/east-west passage work and station-building remodeling, full station improvements were carried out and largely completed on July 29, 2005.

On February 24, 2017, JR East and Morioka Terminal Building announced renovation work on the station and the Fezan building. Fezan phases 1, 2 and 3 opened on March 17, April 28 and late May 2017. On August 31, 2018, "Iwate Galaxy no Shiori" exhibits were installed at the 1st-floor south exit and Taki-no-Hiroba, completing the renovation.

Basement
The former conventional-line underground ticket gate was closed, and the underground passage inside the gate was refurbished as Morioka City's east-west free passage.

At the same time, the underground mall "Morioka Station Department Store Palmo" was renovated; operating company Morioka Station Building was absorbed into Morioka Terminal Building and the name unified as the station building "Fezan".

1st floor
Only the IGR Morioka station remains on the 1st floor; the former JR area was redeveloped ahead of schedule as a shopping zone for convenience stores, souvenirs and light food, and the south side was added as a books-and-household-goods shopping zone, both becoming part of Fezan. Only the View Plaza Morioka floor (no overseas travel, run by View Travel Service) remained as a 1st-floor JR facility.

On March 17, 2017, the IGR/Hanawa Line gate was renovated, and from July 3 to late September 2017 the entrance was renovated.

2nd floor
JR Morioka functions (except View Plaza) moved up from the 1st floor and were consolidated. The previously separate north/south and Fezan-guchi Shinkansen/conventional gates and the south transfer gate (the north transfer gate had closed when the Shinkansen extended to Hachinohe) were consolidated centrally, and a new central conventional-line footbridge built; the old north/south footbridges were closed (the north footbridge was repurposed as the east-west free passage "Sansa Komichi"; the closed south footbridge is used as a warehouse).

Gates were thus consolidated to one point on the 2nd floor, with Shinkansen and conventional gates arranged north and south around the Shinkansen transfer gate; escalators and wheelchair lifts were installed to all Shinkansen and conventional platforms. The escalators near the north gate were renovated on March 17, 2017.

Notes
The pre-renovation north/south footbridges had reverse-flap departure signs installed around 1981, retaining many pre-Shinkansen displays; as station improvements progressed, the north side was replaced by LED signs (moved to the central footbridge) and the south side closed with the footbridge in late July 2005.

When the central footbridge opened, the southern conventional footbridge was taken out of service and fully closed (demolition planned; the Iwate Prefectural Police railway squad box was also to move into the central concourse). The northern side was transferred to Morioka City and converted to the east-west free passage, with tenants moving into the former Fezan-guchi gate site.

From October 1, 2007, widening work on the 2nd-floor east-west free passage (abolishing the paid-area passage on the south side of the footbridge and widening from 3 m to 6 m) was carried out, completed June 13, 2009. From that date the 6 m-wide passage opened fully (though the western portion used as a bicycle parking area remained closed even after the prefab construction office was removed). The nickname "Sansa Komichi" was chosen by public contest.

In summer 2009, a staircase to the 1st floor was added on the north side of the former mezzanine toilet space, giving direct access from Sansa Komichi and the JR north gate to the IGR gate without detour.

日文.首段:
茂市駅（もいちえき）は、岩手県宮古市茂市にある、東日本旅客鉄道（JR東日本）山田線の駅。

2014年3月31日までは、当駅から岩泉線が分岐していた。

章节.歴史:
1934年（昭和9年）11月6日：開業。
 1942年（昭和17年）6月25日：小本線（のちの岩泉線）開業。同線との乗換駅となる。
 1946年（昭和21年）11月26日：風水害により、山田線・小本線とも不通になる。
 1949年（昭和24年）3月5日：山田線の蟇目駅までと小本線が復旧。
 1953年（昭和28年）3月25日：山田線の腹帯駅までが復旧。
 1982年（昭和57年）11月15日：貨物の取り扱いを廃止。
 1984年（昭和59年）2月1日：荷物扱い廃止。
 1987年（昭和62年）4月1日：国鉄分割民営化に伴い、JR東日本の駅となる。
 2010年（平成22年）
 7月31日：災害により、岩泉線が不通となる。
 8月2日：代行バスによる運行開始。
 2014年（平成26年）4月1日：岩泉線廃止。
 2018年（平成30年）
 3月25日：盛岡 - 宮古間の閉塞方式が連査閉塞式から特殊自動閉塞式に変更される。同時に1番線の使用が停止、2面3線から1面2線となる。
 4月22日：盛岡 - 宮古間のCTC化に伴い、終日無人化。宮古駅長の管理下となった。
 2019年（平成31年）3月23日：宮古駅の三陸鉄道への移管に伴い、盛岡駅長の管理下に変更。
 2021年（令和3年）2月下旬：新駅舎の供用開始。
章节.駅構造:

中文.首段:
茂市站（）是位于岩手县宫古市茂市，东日本旅客铁道（JR东日本）的山田线车站。

在2014年3月31日前，此站可转乘岩泉线。

章节.历史:
1934年（昭和9年）11月6日：车站启用。
 1942年（昭和17年）6月25日：小本线（后来为岩泉线）开通，使此站变为转乘站。
 1946年（昭和21年）11月26日：风灾与水灾的影响下，山田线和小本线不能通行。
 1949年（昭和24年）3月5日：山田线此站至蟇目站之间与小本线重开。
 1953年（昭和28年）3月25日：山田线此站至腹带站之间重开。
 1987年（昭和62年）4月1日：伴随国铁分割民营化，车站由东日本旅客铁道（JR东日本）营运。
 2010年（平成22年）
 7月31日：受到天灾影响下，岩泉线不能通行。
 8月2日：开始安排代行巴士服务。
 2014年（平成26年）4月1日：岩泉线废止。
 2018年（平成30年）
 3月25日：盛冈至宫古之间的闭塞方式由连查闭塞式变为特殊自动闭塞式。同时1号月台停止使用。月台配置由2面3线变为1面2线。
 4月22日：盛冈至宫古之间CTC化。此站整日成为无人车站。此站由宫古站长管理。
 2019年（平成31年）3月23日：随著宫古站由三陆铁道管理，此站由盛冈站长管理。
 2021年（令和3年）2月下旬：新车站大楼开始使用。
章节.车站构造:
车站是一座地面车站，设有1面2线的岛式月台，可进行列车交会。原本此站另外设有1面1线的单式月台（1号月台），该月台原本为岩泉线月台（在岩泉线废止后，月台用作到发列车之用）。后来由于闭塞方式改为特殊自动闭塞化，停止使用1号月台。现时于此站到发的列车会使用3号月台。跨线桥已经封闭。1号月台遗址建设了新车站大楼与站内平交道。

在CTC化前。此站是直营车站（设有站长）。当时设有柜台，而运输事务室位于2、3号月台上。当时车站也管理山田线的腹带站和蟇目站。现时此站是无人车站，由盛冈站管理。

岩泉线列车会在此站取得电气路签，然后从1号月台出发。宫古方向的岩泉线直通列车会在1号月台出发。而盛冈方向的岩泉线直通列车（秘境站号等临时列车）方面，由于没有连接盛冈与岩泉方向的渡线，因此当列车停靠此站后，离开此站时先继续前往宫古一方，然后折返返回盛冈方向。因此，实际上临时列车停靠此站的时间会比较长。

英文.首段: Moichi Station (茂市駅) is a railway station on the Yamada Line in Moichi, Miyako, Iwate Prefecture, Japan, operated by East Japan Railway Company (JR East). Until March 31, 2014, the Iwaizumi Line branched off here.

章节.Lines:
Moichi Station is served by the Yamada Line, and is located 87.0 kilometers from the terminus of the line at Morioka Station. It was also a terminal station for the Iwaizumi Line, until its operations were suspended on 31 July 2010 due to a landslide, and the line was closed on 1 April 2014, due to very low public demand.

Station layout
Moichi Station has a one island platform and two tracks. connecting to station building by a footbridge. The station is Unstaffed from 2018.
章节.History:
November 6, 1934: Opened.
June 25, 1942: Kōmotō Line (later Iwaizumi Line) opened; became an interchange station.
November 26, 1946: Both the Yamada and Kōmotō lines suspended by wind/flood damage.
March 5, 1949: Yamada Line restored as far as Hikime, and the Kōmotō Line restored.
March 25, 1953: Yamada Line restored as far as Haratai.
November 15, 1982: Freight handling discontinued.
February 1, 1984: Baggage handling discontinued.
April 1, 1987: Became a JR East station upon JNR privatization.
July 31, 2010: Iwaizumi Line suspended by disaster.
August 2, 2010: Replacement bus operation began.
April 1, 2014: Iwaizumi Line closed.
March 25, 2018: Block system between Morioka and Miyako changed from tablet to special automatic; Platform 1 taken out of use, reducing from two platforms three tracks to one platform two tracks.
April 22, 2018: Became fully unstaffed with CTC; came under Miyako stationmaster.
March 23, 2019: With transfer of Miyako Station to Sanriku, came under Morioka stationmaster.
Late February 2021: New station building entered service.

章节.Station layout:
At-grade station with one island platform serving two tracks, capable of train crossings. It originally also had a side platform facing the building (Platform 1), used by Iwaizumi Line trains (after the line closed, by Miyako–Moichi shuttles), but this was taken out of use during special-automatic-block rationalization and Moichi-origin trains moved to Platform 3. The footbridge was closed; the building is now connected to the platforms by a new foot crossing on the site of the former Platform 1 and on the Morioka side of platforms 2/3.

Until CTC it was a directly managed station (with stationmaster) having a ticket window and an operation office on platforms 2/3; it supervised Haratai and Hikime. It is now an unstaffed station managed from Morioka.

Iwaizumi Line trains took the staff token from the on-duty stationmaster and departed from Platform 1. Through Miyako–Iwaizumi trains could run through Platform 1, but through Morioka–Iwaizumi trains (such as the "Hikyō-eki-gō" extras) had to reverse because there was no Morioka-side to Iwaizumi-side connecting track: after entering the arrival platform, doors were closed and the train moved beyond the Miyako-side points. Such extras therefore dwelled here for a little over 20 minutes.

Platforms

Platform 3 has a departure signal in the Miyako direction and can turn back.

英文.首段: Hikime Station (蟇目駅) is a railway station on the Yamada Line in Hikime, Miyako, Iwate Prefecture, Japan, operated by East Japan Railway Company (JR East).

章节.Lines:
Hikime Station is served by the Yamada Line, and is located 91.5 rail kilometers from the terminus of the line at Morioka Station.

Station layout
Hikime Station has a single side platform serving a  single bi-directional track. There is no longer a station building, but only a waiting room built on the platform. The station is unattended.
章节.History:
November 6, 1934: Opened.
November 26, 1946: Wind/flood damage suspended the section from here to Hirakado.
March 5, 1949: Restored as far as Moichi.
November 1, 1961: Freight handling discontinued.
November 15, 1982: Baggage handling discontinued; station became unstaffed and simply entrusted (later discontinued).
April 1, 1987: Became a JR East station upon JNR privatization.

英文.全文:
Rikuchū-Kawai Station (陸中川井駅) is a railway station on the Yamada Line in Kawai, Miyako, Iwate Prefecture, Japan, operated by East Japan Railway Company (JR East). It stands in the center of the former Kawai village.

History
November 30, 1933: Opened; Rikuchū-Kawai locomotive stabling point established in the yard.
November 16, 1934: Rikuchū-Kawai locomotive stabling point abolished.
November 26, 1946: Suspended by wind/flood damage.
November 21, 1954: Restored.
September 20, 1982: Freight handling discontinued.
November 15, 1982: Baggage handling discontinued; station became unstaffed and simply entrusted; Rikuchū-Kawai stationmaster abolished and the station came under Kawauchi stationmaster.
April 1, 1987: Became a JR East station upon JNR privatization.
April 22, 2018: Simple entrustment ended; station became unstaffed; with unmanning of Kawauchi, came under Miyako stationmaster.
March 23, 2019: With transfer of Miyako Station management to Sanriku, came under Morioka stationmaster.

Station layout
At-grade station with one side platform serving one track. It was formerly a two-platform three-track passing station; the former Platform 1 (down main) is now in use.

Unstaffed. The station office portion houses Kawai Taxi (Kawai Kotsu); it previously handled ticket sales under simple entrustment. The building is similar to Kawauchi Station.
